headline: 4 family members killed in Rangpur, bodies found in locked house
summary: A retired teacher, his wife, and two children were found dead in their home in Kamal Kachna Machhuapara village. Police suspect a robbery-turned-murder.
details: Four members of a family were found dead in a three-story building in Kamal Kachna Machhuapara village of Rangpur city. The bodies were discovered by locals and police on Saturday night around 8:30 PM.

The deceased have been identified as Ganapati Chakraborty (65), a retired teacher of Rangpur Zilla School, and his wife Pritilata Chakraborty (50), their son Ayush Chakraborty (14), and daughter Agami Chakraborty (28).
Rangpur CID police Inspector Abu Hasan Kabir confirmed the recovery of the bodies, noting that a strong odor had spread throughout the building, indicating the deaths occurred several days prior.
Kotwali Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) AKM Nazmul Kader stated that the murders are believed to have taken place two to three days before the discovery.

CID officer-in-charge Sumit Chowdhury visited the scene and told reporters that the evidence suggests a robbery. He noted that the house's electrical connection had been disconnected and areas where money was kept had been ransacked.
According to investigators, it appears the victims were strangled with ropes or towels. Police are currently investigating the case to identify and apprehend the culprits.
caption:
A retired teacher, his wife, and two children found dead in their locked home in Rangpur. Police suspect robbery.

Four members of a family were found dead in a three-story building in Kamal Kachna Machhuapara village of Rangpur city. The bodies were discovered by locals and police on Saturday night around 8:30 PM.

The deceased have been identified as Ganapati Chakraborty (65), a retired teacher of Rangpur Zilla School, and his wife Pritilata Chakraborty (50), their son Ayush Chakraborty (14), and daughter Agami Chakraborty (28).

Rangpur CID police Inspector Abu Hasan Kabir confirmed the recovery of the bodies, noting that a strong odor had spread throughout the building, indicating the deaths occurred several days prior.

Kotwali Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) AKM Nazmul Kader stated that the murders are believed to have taken place two to three days before the discovery.

CID officer-in-charge Sumit Chowdhury visited the scene and told reporters that the evidence suggests a robbery. He noted that the house's electrical connection had been disconnected and areas where money was kept had been ransacked.

According to investigators, it appears the victims were strangled with ropes or towels. Police are currently investigating the case to identify and apprehend the culprits.

headline: Fear grips city as muggings surge across Dhaka
summary: Residents report increasing incidents of street crime, leaving many in fear for their safety.
details: Street crime has seen a significant increase in the capital city, with muggings becoming more frequent across various neighborhoods.
Residents have expressed growing anxiety over their safety, reporting a rise in bold and brazen incidents of theft and robbery.
The surge in muggings has left many citizens feeling vulnerable, particularly during late hours or in less crowded areas.
Local authorities are being urged to increase patrols and implement stricter security measures to combat the rising crime wave.
